bullets.title: META: Samsung $6.54B MTIA chip deal, cloud compute launch, AI slower than expected
bullets.body: Bloomberg/SED reported Samsung Foundry in talks with Meta for a KRW10T+ (~$6.54B) contract to mass-produce Meta's 3rd-gen MTIA custom AI chip. Simultaneously, Meta announced plans to launch 'Meta Compute' cloud business—selling excess AI compute capacity and hosted model access—which drove shares ~9% higher July 1. Zuckerberg separately acknowledged in an internal town hall that AI agent development has proceeded slower than expected over the past four months, with structural changes not yet delivering results. MS estimates every 250MW leased at $40/Watt adds ~$3 (~8%) to 2028 EPS; Citi reiterates Buy at $850 PT; JPM downgraded to Neutral (from OW) on April 30 at $725 PT, preferring Meta focus on its 4B user base.

bullets.title: META Pocket app + RBLX bear read; APP initiated strong buy
bullets.body: Meta launched 'Pocket,' a new social app featuring a social feed of vibe-coded mini games, which Citi flagged as potentially negative for Roblox. Separately, Raymond James initiated AppLovin (APP) at strong buy with $640 PT citing e-commerce advertising growth opportunity; APP rose ~10% on risk-on sentiment. UBS ad checks show AMZN DSP and APP as standout winners while TTD, SNAP, PINS remain under pressure from brand-spend weakness.

bullets.title: MU: UBS raises 2H26 DRAM/NAND price forecasts; $1,625 PT; memory stocks down 17% from June peak
bullets.body: UBS raised 2H26 DDR contract pricing to +32% QoQ in 3Q26 (vs +17% prior) and NAND to +30% QoQ (vs +17% prior); DRAM seen undersupplied until at least 2Q28 with 2027 bit demand growth of +36.2% vs supply of +19.3%. Memory industry revenues forecast at $992bn in 2026 and $1.76tn in 2027 with ~$1.2tn FCF in 2027E. Micron rated Buy with $1,625 PT; KeyBanc maintains Overweight at $1,600 PT. Memory stocks pulled back ~17% from June peak, viewed as temporary on strong fundamentals; pullback widely attributed to Meta cloud/overcapacity narrative and quarter-end rebalancing.

bullets.title: NVDA: Revenue-sharing model for AI clouds; SOX +88% in Q2; semis sold off on Meta capex narrative
bullets.body: Nvidia launched a revenue-sharing/credit-support model with AI cloud partners (DSX AI factories), deploying GB300 GPUs at partners like Sharon AI and Firimus. NVDA NDR with CEO Jensen Huang and CFO Colette Kress scheduled July 8-9 (Morgan Stanley). The SOX index posted +88% in Q2 2026, best quarter since index inception in 1993, though it fell sharply (~6-10%) the week of July 1 as Meta's cloud announcement sparked overbuild fears. JPM's AI infrastructure TAM model was revised: servers +9/+12/+20% for 2026/27/28; NVDA holds ~50% AI DC switch share.

bullets.title: CRWV/NBIS: Heavy selling on Meta cloud announcement; exposure highlighted as existential risk
bullets.body: CoreWeave (CRWV) and Nebius (NBIS) fell 13-17% on July 1-2 after Meta announced 'Meta Compute,' as META is ~33% and >50% of CRWV and NBIS backlogs respectively. DA Davidson flagged this as 'materially negative' for both names if Meta scales back compute ambitions. Jefferies maintained Buy on META at $825 PT, arguing the neocloud play boosts ROIC and doesn't signal a capex pullback. CRWV hit 52-week lows in Canada.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone 17 production cuts; Chinese memory supplier talks; EU/CMA regulatory pressure
bullets.body: Apple reduced iPhone 17 production plans on weaker shipment forecasts. Apple is in talks with sanctioned Chinese memory suppliers CXMT and YMTC to offset surging DRAM/NAND costs, while lobbying the White House for political cover. Apple raised Mac/iPad prices 15-25% citing component cost surge. Apple sought to avoid EU fines over delayed Siri AI launch (Cook holding talks with EU tech chief). UK CMA progressing work on WebKit restrictions. UBS models iPhone margins dropping to 36.4%/35.9% without pricing relief; Wedbush maintains $400 PT, Morgan Stanley maintains $360 PT.

bullets.title: TSLA: Record Q2 deliveries +25% YoY; energy storage beats; FSD Europe progress
bullets.body: Tesla reported Q2 deliveries of ~480K vehicles (+25% YoY, +34% QoQ), beating ~406K consensus (Citi had ~397K). Energy storage at 13.5 GWh (+34% YoY) was slightly below Morgan Stanley's 13.9GWh estimate but ahead of consensus. MS noted demand is robust from improving unit economics at utility-scale ESS and data centers. Tesla also cut employee AI spending to $200/week starting July 6. US June auto SAAR hit 16.5mn units, beating estimates, with Tesla posting ~37K US units (-27% YoY).

bullets.title: CMCSA: NBCUniversal spin-off announced; upgrades from Deutsche Bank and Rosenblatt
bullets.body: Comcast announced a tax-free spin-off of NBCUniversal and Sky into a separate public company, expected to complete in ~12 months. Mike Cavanagh will lead NBCU; Michael Angelakis to lead Comcast RemainCo (cable/connectivity). Deutsche Bank upgraded CMCSA to Buy (PT $32, 32% upside); Rosenblatt upgraded to Buy (PT $31). Wolfe Research called the spin a strategic precursor to potential CMCSA-CHTR cable merger, with NBCU potentially attracting Netflix as a buyer. CMCSA opened +22% Monday June 29 on spin announcement. UBS maintains Neutral, noting media assets trading at 0-3x EBITDA vs. peer range of 8-13x.

bullets.title: FOXA: Wolfe upgrades to Outperform at $71 PT post-Roku deal; TV ratings surge on World Cup/NBA
bullets.body: Wolfe upgraded Fox Corp to Outperform from Peer Perform with $71 PT (36% upside), arguing the Roku acquisition doubles Fox's long-term sales CAGR and shifts narrative to multi-channel CTV growth. FOXA had fallen 23% since the June 15 deal announcement. Pro forma FOXA trades at 11.8x NTM UFCF. UBS TV ratings data showed Fox/FS1 up 127% YoY in the week due to World Cup; FS1 World Cup group stage estimated to generate ~$500M in advertising revenue for Fox. WBD viewership down 21% in Q2 due to NBA lap.

bullets.title: DLR: $7.8B Blackstone data center acquisition; 80bps 2027 FFO accretion; stock -4.5%
bullets.body: Digital Realty announced the acquisition of Blackstone's interest in three fully-leased Northern Virginia hyperscale data centers (288 MW) at $7.8B gross value ($3.5B cash+stock to Blackstone), >6.5% initial cap rate with 3.6% annual escalators. Deal expected accretive ~80bps Core FFOPS in 2027, ~330bps in 2028. Citi maintains Buy at $226 PT. KeyBanc views as first JV buyback at reasonable valuations. DLR stock was down ~4-5% post-announcement on dilution from $2.3B secondary.

bullets.title: BE: $25B Brookfield AI infrastructure partnership 5x expansion; MS upgrades to OW at $310 PT
bullets.body: Bloom Energy and Brookfield expanded their AI infrastructure partnership from $5B to $25B (potential 5 GW of fuel cell capacity). Morgan Stanley upgraded BE to Overweight with $310 PT, noting BE has ~2.5 GW of project wins with AEP, ORCL, and NBIS, and the Brookfield confidence validates BE's time-to-power advantage. UBS raised PT to $355 from $322. BE surged ~9-10% on June 29-30.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Morgan Stanley raises PT to $415 on 9GW 2028 compute; EU €4.1B antitrust fine upheld
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised GOOGL PT to $415 from $375, modeling 9 GW incremental compute capacity in 2028 with 4 GW TPU sold on a 1P basis, driving Google Cloud to $300B+ revenue in 2028 at 106%/44% growth in 2027/2028. Capex raised to $350B/$375B for 2027/2028. Separately, the EU Court of Justice upheld Google's €4.13B ($4.70B) Android antitrust fine, and a Swedish court ordered Google to pay Klarna $1.97B in antitrust damages.

bullets.title: PLTR: DA Davidson upgrades to Buy at $175 PT; NVDA Nemotron partnership
bullets.body: DA Davidson upgraded Palantir to Buy from Neutral with PT raised to $175 (from $165), citing 2x faster growth than peers at in-line valuation (down from 200x to 50x EV/Sales), unique moat combining disparate data sources via Forward Deployed Engineers, and FCF margins doubling annually. Palantir also launched an engine for deploying NVIDIA Nemotron open-source AI models in sovereign environments.

bullets.title: ADBE: HSBC upgrades to Buy at $308 PT; DA Davidson reiterated Buy; AI disruption fears 'overdone'
bullets.body: HSBC upgraded Adobe to Buy from Hold, raising PT to $308 from $282 (46% upside from ~$211), with analyst Stephen Bersey arguing AI disruption fears are overdone and there is no evidence of market share loss. ADBE was also up ~1.9% in pre-market July 2 on the upgrade news.

bullets.title: NOW/CRM: Guggenheim upgrades both to Buy; AI bear case called 'hallucination'
bullets.body: Guggenheim upgraded Salesforce (CRM) to Buy from Neutral with $228 PT (46% upside) and ServiceNow (NOW) to Buy from Neutral with $125 PT (26% upside). Analyst John DiFucci argued the AI bear case for software is overblown, current valuations imply perpetual decline that is not expected, and both companies should see subscription revenue stabilization in 2026 with potential acceleration in late 2026/2027. CRM's Agentforce ARR hit $1.2B in Q1 FY27 (+205% YoY).

bullets.title: HOOD: Perpetual futures launch in EU; Mizuho raises PT to $130 on global hyperscaler thesis
bullets.body: Robinhood launched perpetual futures on real-world assets (gold, silver, oil, ETFs, FX) in Europe via Bitstamp with up to 10x leverage. Mizuho raised HOOD PT to $130 from $115, framing the company as potentially the first global online brokerage 'hyperscaler' with 27M+ funded accounts and Gen-Z appeal expanding into Canada, UK, Asia. Piper Sandler reiterates Overweight at $135 PT. HOOD surged +19.8% on the week on perpetual futures news and strong equity/options/crypto volumes. Stock added to Mizuho's July Top Picks.

bullets.title: DKNG: 2Q EBITDA estimates lowered to $222M from $265M; NY OSB GGR +86% YoY on World Cup
bullets.body: Citi lowered DraftKings 2Q adj EBITDA to $222M (from $265M) due to DraftKings Predictions marketing spend timing (pulled into 2Q vs expected 2H), but maintains Buy at $30 PT with FY adj EBITDA of $787M ahead of Street's $767M. NY OSB data showed week-ending 6/28 GGR +86% YoY (handle +47% YoY) boosted by World Cup; 2QTD GGR -12% YoY on tougher holds. DraftKings launched DKeX prediction markets exchange with $3.4B annualized volume.

bullets.title: VZ/T: BT JV announcement drives VZ -5%; Starlink-Charter mobile talks weigh on sector
bullets.body: Verizon announced a 50:50 joint venture with BT Group for international business, recording $700-800M in Q2 charges including an $800M loss. VZ fell ~5% on the news. Charter was reportedly in exec-level talks with SpaceX on a consumer mobile phone partnership using Spectrum's ground infrastructure. Both CMCSA and CHTR surged on spin/SpaceX news. Wolfe Research sees TMUS (Outperform, $255 PT) as the preferred telecom with superior service revenue growth; sector broadly -21% over past 3 months on Starlink fears.

bullets.title: SMCI: Taiwan offices raided in chip-smuggling probe; stock -8.1%
bullets.body: Taiwanese authorities raided Super Micro Computer's offices as part of an expanded investigation into alleged smuggling of NVIDIA chips into China. SMCI fell -8.1% on June 29 with DELL and HPE trading higher in sympathy. SMCI was also flagged for raising up to $7B to fund components for ~$39B in AI server orders.

bullets.title: SHOP: +4.8% on broad market recovery; BABA: $600M DOJ settlement, Claude ban, insider sale
bullets.body: Shopify traded +4.8-5.1% in Canadian markets during the week on broader tech recovery. Alibaba agreed to pay $600M to settle a DOJ probe over illegal substance sales on its payment platform (AUS Merchant Services). Alibaba also banned employee use of Anthropic's Claude Code citing security concerns, after Anthropic accused Alibaba of illicitly accessing its models via fake accounts. Alibaba President Michael Evans sold 720K shares at $95.98 on June 29.
